opinions.rationale: The future-conditioning mechanism under random-order sampling without replacement is correct, and chronological sampling can exhaust sparse matching strata at high sampling ratios. The statement nevertheless overreaches. Bias is undefined until a target comparator distribution, outcome scale, and effect estimand are specified; differences between sampled cohorts are not automatically causal-effect bias. Exhaustion is not unique to chronological sampling, and sampling with replacement guarantees matches only in strata containing at least one eligible comparator. The alternative cohorts are also not intrinsically counterfactual or unavailable: when the source registry and sampling frame are retained, all schemes can be rerun before effect estimation. Known inclusion probabilities, standardization, or selection weighting can address some sampling effects when the necessary frame variables, outcome information, positivity, and identifying assumptions hold. Nonparametric recovery generally fails only when the analyst retains the realized cohort without adequate frame information or when relevant target strata have zero inclusion probability. Conversely, no nontrivial universal bound can be obtained from the sampling ratio, aggregate pool ratio, and marginal baseline hazard alone. Joint information about index dates, matching strata, eligibility histories, survival, competing events, and outcome risk is required; distributions sharing the proposed three summaries can produce different directions and magnitudes. A useful calibration method under explicit assumptions remains an open roadmap item, but the asserted universal absence of procedures and downstream remedies is false, and the severity is substantial only for high sampling fractions in sparse, high-risk strata.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: In matched external-comparator designs with high sampling fractions, random-order sampling without replacement can select on future survival or event-free status, while chronological sampling without replacement can deplete sparse matching strata. If only the realized matched cohort is retained and no adequate sampling-frame information or identifying assumptions are available, the comparator risk under an alternative scheme is not point identified. No nontrivial universal bound follows from the sampling ratio, aggregate pool ratio, and marginal baseline hazard alone. Analysts should retain the source frame, prespecify and report the scheme and unmatched counts, rerun feasible schemes, and use design-based adjustment or sensitivity analysis when its assumptions are supportable.
